Pali utupariṇāma, change of season, as a source of disease, e.g. (vedayitāni …) utupariṇāma-jāni (comm. = utupariṇāmato atisīta-atiuṇha-ututo jātāni); ṛtupariṇāmāye, (wrongly), or ṛtuvipari˚, perh. adj. subject to change of season; or, prob. reading ˚nāma-tāye, because of change of season?; in vipācanīye grahaṇīye samanvāgatā nāpy atiśītāye nāpy atiuṣṇāye ( na cāti˚ both times) ṛtu- ( ṛtu-vi-)pariṇāmāye. A like passage reads, instead of ṛtu(vi)pari˚, in the mss. samāye cintamatāye (v.l. vinta˚), which is obscure; em. sammāpariṇāmāye, but this seems violent; samāye seems sound, as it occurs just before. understands this as causing good digestion, and infers that ṛtu-pari˚ means the same. He does not mention, which reads vipariṇāma; this, unlike pariṇāma, seems never to be used in Skt., Pali or Pkt. in the sense of digestion; and the established Pali cpd. utu-pariṇāma certainly goes against ʼs view. The only question is, can ṛtupariṇāmāye, fem., be an adj. going with grahaṇīye, or should we take it as a noun? In the latter case an em. to ˚matāye seems probable.

(= avi-rajas, q.v.), lit. sheep-speck, a small unit of matter; like avi-rajas, it occurs and in tabular lists of very small weights or measures; in all three, seven śaśa-rajāṃsi (q.v.) make one eḍaka-(avi-)r˚ and seven of these make one go-rajas (q.v.). Acc. to, cited by, the mg. is said by Hiuen Tsʼang and a Chin. transl. of to be a grain of dust on the hide of a hare (sheep, beeve). But Tib. on both and says simply hare- (sheep-, cow-)speck (rdul); to be sure, s.v. rdul declares that glaṅ rdul means a mote in the dung of an ox, a small particle of cowdung. But this, as well as the different guess from Chin., can hardly be anything but implausible guesswork. Why should a speck on the skin, or in the dung, of an animal vary with the size of the animal? The Tib. itself gives no such indication. It seems safe to assume that hare-speck, sheep-speck, and cow-speck mean only three different sizes of small particles.

, taken by as ppp. of ava with root kas (see), gone down, descended. I cannot improve on this suggestion, altho no form of this cpd. has been recorded elsewhere. Usually with acc. or loc. of that to (sometimes into) which the subject has gone down, the pple. ˚to or ˚tā being a periphrasis for a past tense: to the sea, in order to embark,; to a river, (to draw water);; to a pool, (by a staircase, sopānena), 15;;; from the Himalayan region into another country (text uncertain), 12; to the bazaar-street;; from a wagon; a nāga enters into the Buddhaʼs alms-bowl,. Not found outside of.

, m. (= aukarika, q.v.; acc. to, = Tib. yul tsoṅ [read tshoṅ] pa, see below), some kind of tradesman;, ‘country merchant’; but yul, which indeed often means janapada (opp. to town), in comp. with tshoṅ pa, merchant, could possibly mean dealer in agricultural products, something like truck-farmer; possibly cf. ogara, oggara, cited by from Prākṛta-piṅgala as meaning a king of grain or rice. Certainly not a keeper of a shop in the country, for the story shows that it means a member of an urban tradesmanʼs guild, parallel with perfumers: pitā te okkarika āsīd; [Page158-1b] tenaukkarikāpaṇo vyavasthāpitaḥ; tenaukkarika-tvaṃ tyaktvā. The story is the same as that in which uses aukarika. I see no reason to associate with either of these words the n. pr. Utkarika or Otk˚, qq.v.

(for ava-kṣ˚, caus. to Skt. apa-kṣi), causes to be done away with, orders put away, with ‘inner accusative’ vadham, to death, i.e. orders executed: (prose), read with 5 of 6 mss. (aparādhaṃ ca ananuyujyā, read ˚jya, q.v.) vadham okṣapayanti (one ms. ākṣap˚; em. ākṣep˚).
, nt. (= Pali id.; Skt. ava-ga˚ not in this sense), going down, setting (of heavenly bodies): (prose; candrasūryāṇāṃ …) ogamanāni.

, m., one who grasps (intellectually), acquires (knowledge): (vs) ogrāhako ca paripṛcchamāno (… evaṃkaro prajñāvāṃ bhoti). Prob. false Sktization of Pali uggāhako (vā paripucchako siyā, same line as above,). Alternatively, might be false Sktization of a Pali *ogāhaka to ogāhati, ˚heti (= Skt. ava-gāh-), penetrates (used once with object lokanāthassa sāsanaṃ,).

, m. (= Pali id.), flood (of evils, passions, or depravities, ‘crossing’ of which, tar- or ut-tar-, is necessary for salvation); usually four in number, presumably as in Pali = the 4 āsrava or yoga, qq.v. (cf. āśravaḥ, oghaḥ): catur-ogha-pāra-gāmitābhiprāyasya (bodhisattvasya) (read so with Tib. pha rol tu ḥgro baḥi bsam pa can, intending to go to the further shore …; best ms. A ˚pāramitābhi˚, with others ˚pāragāminābhi˚); (vs) ogha catvāri tīrtvā; caturoghottīrṇānāṃ (Buddhānāṃ);; sattvānāṃ caturoghottaraṇatāyai; five or six ogha, (vs) pañcoghatīrṇo taratīha ṣaṣṭhaṃ (text ṣaṣṭaṃ; = Pali; cf.,; it is not clear what these are; for one not very plausible conjecture see s.v.).

= ojas, strength, in Bhvr. cpds.: [Page159-a] (prose) alpaujaskau; (vs) anojasko (mss. anau˚); (vs) svabhāva-saujaska-.

(= Pali id.; derived by and from Skt. ūrj, by from ojas, which seems more plausible), food: = (prose) (lābhinī bhavati divyānāṃ gandhānāṃ … mālyānāṃ … vilepanānāṃ) divyānāṃ ojānām; (and 6) (prose) (vayaṃ te romakūpa- [mss. ˚pe] vivarāntareṣu) divyām ojām adhyohariṣyāmaḥ; see s.v. adhyoharati (used in Pali, like its noun ajjhohāra, of food). It seems clear that in BHS, at least, ojā means simply food, not essence or the like.
(for Ojaḥpati), n. of one of 4 (masc.) devatās of the Bodhivṛkṣa: (so all mss.; em. Ojāpati). Cf. next.
, n. of one of 8 (fem.) devatās of the Bodhivṛkṣa:. Cf. prec.; but there is otherwise no resemblance between the two lists.
, adj. compv. (cf. Pali ojavant(a), Vedic ojasvant; in Skt. only ojasvin), strong-er: (vs) ojovantatarā bhonti lakṣmīvīryabalānvitāḥ.

, adj. and subst. (f. ˚rī), lit. strength-robber; ep. of rākṣasas: rākṣasa eva ojohāra ihāgacchati; of yakṣas, ojohārāḥ pañca yakṣāḥ; subst. m. and f., in a list of evil supernatural beings, ojohāro vaujohārī vā;. Cf. next two. See also s.v. 2 -hāra; in both and the mg. to rob the strength (of people) would be possible.

, adj. or subst. m. (cf. prec., but see also s.v. 2 -hāra, hāraka), strength-robbing, -robber; or, as expression of purpose, to rob the strength (of people):, said of the 1000 sons of a yakṣiṇī: te 'pi vaiśāliṃ ojohārakā preṣitā, vaiśālim gatvā manuṣyāṇām ojaṃ haranti (so that they all became sick).
(cf. prec. two), n. of a piśācī:.

(in mg. 2 = Pali id.; in mg. 1 seemingly = Pali uḍḍeti, very rare, only 1 reasonably clear case, bhikkhu sikkāya pattaṃ uḍḍitvā, text uṭṭitvā, see), (1) ties, fastens (on): (see Crit. (= Pali id., Skt. avara), hither, nearer, or lower; in ora-pāra (Pali id.), the nearer and the farther (state of existence), substantially the present life and any future life: so bhikṣu jahāti orapāraṃ = Pali so bhikkhu etc.
(ava plus Skt. ravati; not recorded elsewhere), murmurs, complains: (prose) (rājñā …) śabdāpito putro (so with mss.): jānapadā oravanti, … the people of the country are complaining.

, adj., perhaps for ava-ruṇḍa = ruṇḍa, mutilated (cf. ava-kubja, ava-koṭimaka): (vs) chinna-kara-caraṇa ivoruṇḍaḥ, mutilated, as if having hands and feet cut off. But possibly understand ivo (m.c. for iva,) ruṇḍaḥ; in a verse, the meter of which is MIndic and obscure to me.

(Pali ˚ka, nt., id.), girdle: māṇavaṃ ovaṭṭikāyāṃ (mss.; em. kṛkāṭikāyāṃ) gṛhya; in perhaps read ovaṭṭikāhi (or ˚kehi, nt. as in Pali?) for mss. ovātakehi (āvāpakehi) ratanadāmakehi paṭṭadāmakehi … samalaṃkṛtaṃ bodhivṛkṣaṃ saṃjānetsuḥ.

(so recorded; n. pl.? wrongly divided in Kyoto ed. ovidhya-nakhā; ovidhyana is n. act. from Pali ovijjhati shoots down, to Skt. ava-vyadh), parapet, battlement, lit. holes for shooting (arrows) down: = Tib. mdaḥ yab, or, ba gam, both having substantially this mg., but the first seems to mean lit. arrow-shelter.

, nt. (var. ośaḍuka), prob. some kind of plaster: = Tib. ḥdag rdzas, a kind of clay (dry or wet); Chin. a substance for smearing, or sticky stuff.

(= Pali osadhi), n. or epithet of a particular star: n. sg. ˚dhi or ˚dhī, and (vs) tāravarā va oṣadhī, by ʼs em., which is proved by the Pali parallel. In Pali more often called osadhi-tārakā, star of medicine.

, in (vs) apy oṣitā āmiṣapātracīvare (so apparently divide), set upon, intent upon worldly things (like) bowl and robe (see āmiṣa). Cf. Pali an-osita, not occupied (of houses;). If correct, oṣita seems = Skt. avasita; used with loc. But api at the beginning is suspicious, and s does not normally become ṣ after MIndic o for ava. I suspect corruption.

, adj. (= Skt. avasanna; in this sense, of flowers, not recorded), wilted, of flowers: (vs) osanna-puṣpaṃ jinacetiyeṣu (equivalent to jīrṇaṃ puṣpaṃ, puṣpaṃ purimaṃ milānaṃ, and others in the vicinity).

, nt. (to next; = Pali id.), entrance, approach: osaraṇe (mss. osakaṇe) ca bharitā addaśi pramadā, at the entrance (to the kingʼs palace) … (otherwise); kasya eṣa osaraṇaśabdaḥ (? mss. te saraṇa˚, or te śaraśa˚), whose noise of approach is this? In osaraṇāni, in a line otherwise hopelessly corrupt, corresponds to the same word in the same vs of Pali, the rest of which seems also corrupt (so ed.); the comm. says it means heretical views (ogahanāni titthāni, diṭṭhiyo). ʼs em. and interpretation of the line are unconvincing; but the Pali is also dubious, and its comm. questionable. I cannot solve the problem.

(= Pali id. or avasarati; cf. prec.; see avasarati 1, and for 2 osarati see s.v. avaśirati), (1) enters, approaches, arrives: kumāro siṃhasya va (? mss. ca) osarantasya śabdaṃ śṛṇvati; (vs) na te koṣṭhesmiṃ (so read with 1 ms.) osaranti (the Pali version,, has upenti); (2) caus. osārayati = Pali osāreti, restores (a monk to good standing in the order): osārayantu mām āyuṣmantaḥ;;; osāryate (prose). , also ˚ṇa (= Pali id.; cf. avasāraṇa; to prec., 2, plus -aṇā), restitution (to good standing, of a monk or nun that has been disciplined): ˚ṇāṃ yācantam;; ˚nāṃ yācasva 29a.1; ˚ṇā yācitavyā; ˚ṇaṃ, etc. See also utsāraṇa.
(= Skt. avasupta, see s.v. avasvāpayati), ppp. to osopati, q.v.

, nt. (to prec.; cf. AMg. osovaṇī, profound sleep acc. to), sleep, or putting to sleep: devehi sarvasya janasya … osopanaṃ kṛtaṃ. Cf. also osvāpana, apasvāpana.
, n. of demoniac beings (for *ava-st˚?): omārako vostārako (v.l. vā ost˚); masc. etc.; fem. ˚kī; m. and f. and ostārako vaustārakī vā;.

(presumably for ava-sv˚, to avasvāpayati with -ana; cf. apa-sv˚), going to sleep; sleeping; or perhaps putting to sleep: (vs; avasvāpanaṃ would be metrically better!) devatābhi osvāpanaṃ kṛtam (in the corresponding prose version apasvāpanaṃ); (prose) sarvasya rājakulasya ˚naṃ kṛtam. (m.; perh. cf. AMg. oharai, establish, settle, ‘sthāpan karnā, pratiṣṭhit karnā’; derived by from upa-har-), domicile, abode: te … svakam [Page161-b] ohāraṃ gatā; tato ohārāto (mss. ˚rito) nirgamya;. ohāraṃ prasthito.

(m. or nt.), ? some subject that was part of the education of a brahman: in a list of such, (… upanyastaḥ … samudācāre bhasmagrahe) autkare bhoskāre (mss. bhotk˚) ṛgvede …; same passage reads ḍoṅkāre (for aut˚) bhoṅkāre.

, adj. (cf. Pali oḷāra, once, in gloss on atulaṃ, = appamāṇaṃ oḷāraṃ paṇītaṃ, but would read uḷāraṃ with v.l.; = Skt. udāra, or BHS audārika), (1) large, vast, of radiance, avabhāsa: audāre avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkṛte; cf. udārāvabhāsaḥ, and audārike avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkriyamāṇe; the usual mg. of audārika might suggest material, corporeal, i.e. physically actualized, but the parallels are against this; cf. aprameyasya udārasya ca mahato avabhāsasya …, and similarly in parallels (collected s.v. lokāntarikā); (2) gross, unrefined (= audārika): audārādhimuktikānāṃ viśuddhaye; this cannot = udāra- (tho this is compounded elsewhere with adhimuktika, q.v.) since that is a complimentary term, and this is not (cf. the parallel saṃkliṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ viśuddhaye, and similarly).

, adj. (see also ˚ka-tā; from Skt. udāra plus ika; udāra, audāra, qq.v., also occur rarely, but audarika, q.v., is a false reading for this; = Pali oḷārika), gross; in a list of ‘synonyms for bṛhat’, defined in Tib. by a number of terms including rags pa (text la! corr. in Tib. Index), gross, corporeal, substantial; che ba, great; sbom pa, stout, gross, coarse; also che loṅ, loṅ, and raṅ po, the precise lit. mgs. of which are not clear to me; in the word is nt. and is preceded by udāraḥ, viśālam, vipulam, and followed by pṛthuḥ. Practically all BHS occurrences may be subsumed under the mg. (1) gross, as opposed to sūkṣma, fine, subtle (so in Pali contrasted with sukhuma), -sūkṣmaudārika-; audārikaṃ vā sūkṣmaṃ vā (rūpam); (id.) and 18 (vijñānam); so of the body, gross, substantial, material, devatā sā audārikam ātmabhāvam abhisaṃdarśya; (vs) Puṣyaś ca nakṣatra … ˚kaṃ nirmiṇi ātmabhāvaṃ, Puṣya created by magic a corporeal body; mahādevo … audārikenātmabhāvena sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati; audārikakāya-viheṭhanayā, by injuring the actual, physical body (of creatures); kāyena vā audārikeṇa cāturmahābhūtikena; ayaṃ … kāyo rūpī audārikaś cāturmahābhūtika(ḥ); (Māra says:) mātāpitṛsambhavo śramaṇagautamasya kāyo audāriko (so mss.) … mama punar manomayo kāyo; (a Bodhisattva in speaking to women) nāntaśo dantāvalīm apy upadarśayati, kaḥ punar vāda audārikamukhavikāram, … not to speak of (showing) any (emotional) alteration (due to internal feelings) in his corporeal (gross, external) face; of other things, esp. food, āhāra (also in Pali, where oḷārika āhāra, material or substantial food or sustenance, is contrasted with immaterial kinds of sustenance, see): (na … sukhāvatyāṃ) … sattvā audārika-yūṣa-phāṇīkārāhāram (so ed. em.; mss. corrupt but beginning audāri-)āharanti, api tu … yathārūpam evāhāram ākāṅkṣanti, tathārūpam āhṛtam eva saṃjānanti, prīṇitakāyāś ca bhavanti; in this sense audārika āhāra is always to be understood (not abundant food), etc.; (others, see s.v. audarika); material, corporeal (forms of worship), (a Bodhisattva in the 8th bhūmi) audārikaṃ buddhadarśanapūjopasthānaṃ notsṛjati; others, misc., bodhisattvasyaudārikāṇy … gotraliṅgāni; (2) in a few cases possibly great, large: audārikāś cāsyāśvāsapraśvāsā gurugurukāḥ pravartante yathā meghasya garjaṭo … śabdaḥ, enormous breathings; but since a rākṣasa is being described, perhaps gross, coarse would better correspond to the mg., cf. in Pali assāsapassāsā pi oḷārikā honti, balavatarā huovā pavattanti etc. ( the breathings too are gross etc.); as to audārike avabhāsanimitte, see audāra.
, abstr. to prec., coarseness (Tib. rags pa): sthūlabhittikatā audārikatā.

, nt, (in Skt. only haughtiness: = Pali uddhacca), frivolity, in the double sense of amusement, [Page162-a] idle sport, and mental indolence, lack of seriousness of mind (‘the property antithetical to attention’,; frivolité.): = Tib. rgod pa, laughter (acc. to and also languor, indolence, which the questions); here it stands between asaṃprajanyam aud kaukṛtyam, styānam; (see s.v. drava; here seems clearly related to amusement); see drava also for where read auddhatyaṃ for audatyaṃ (Tib. mig zur gyis lta bar byed, making glances with the corners of the eyes); (said of women) tyakta-vibhrama-vilāsauddhatyā(ḥ); as one of the 6 āvaraṇa (q.v.) to samādhi,; usually assoc. with such qualities as styāna, middha, and esp. kaukṛtya, qq.v., in formulaic lists which hardly give much help,;;;;; auddhatya-kaukṛtya, together, constitute one of the 5 nīvaraṇa, q.v.

, nt. (also udbilya, udvilya, q.v.; these sometimes occur as vv.ll. for aud˚; = Pali ubbilla; acc. to to ud plus vell-; other theories, see), joy, pleasurable excitement: ˚bilya-prāpta, often with adbhuta-p˚,;;;; ˚ya-jāta; ˚ya-kārī (n. sg. ˚kārin); atīvaudbilyam utpannaṃ; cittasya prāmodyaṃ kāyasyaudbilyam (n. sg.); cittaudvilyaprītikaraṇyodārayā prabhayā (cf. under udbilya); cittaudvilyakaraṇī (prabhā).

, adj. (the two forms identical in mg. and both included below; list of occurrences of upapāduka s.v.; aupapādika only, where 2 mss. ˚duka; corresp. to Pali opapātika, Jain Skt. aupa˚, AMg. uvavāia, ˚iya; der. from upapāda, q.v.; with;, I believe BHS shows the etymologically historical form, from upa-pad, contrary to, s.v., and; the counter-argument that upa-pad means to be born in the usual [rather, in any] way is inconclusive, since the passages cited below show that in BHS these words are definitely associated with upa-pad, see esp.;;), born by spontaneous generation: often the fourth of 4 kinds of beings classified as to manner of birth, aṇḍajā(ḥ vā) jārāyujā(ḥ vā) saṃsvedajā(ḥ vā)aupapādukā(ḥ vā),; =;;; or ˚upapādukā(ḥ vā); (v.l. aupa˚); (n. sg. forms); also in cpd. -aṇḍaja-jarāyuja-saṃsvedajaupapāduka-; jarāyujāṇḍajasaṃsvedaja-upapāduka-sattva-; with omission of one member, aṇḍaja, saṃsvedaja, upapāduka,; jarāyuja-saṃsvedajaupapādukānāṃ; sometimes with addition of other terms, as rūpiṇo vārūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vāsaṃjñino vā etc.;, and similar additions in some others of the above; other occurrences: aupapādukāḥ sattvā ghaṭīyantraprayogena cyavamānā upapadyamānāś ca (falling and being reborn in the manner of a bucket-machine, sc. for raising water from a well) kartayvāḥ (as part of the pañcagaṇḍakaṃ, q.v., cakram); usually, as here, of human beings, esp. Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and cakravartins; they often appear sitting on lotuses, which may themselves be spontaneously generated, as in yasmiṃś ca buddhakṣetra upapatsyate tasminn aupapāduke saptaratnamaye padma upapatsyate; (vs; in 3 ‘there is no sexual intercourse’) upapāduka te jinorasāḥ padmagarbheṣu niṣaṇṇa nirmalāḥ; te (bodhisattvāḥ) tatra nānāraṅgeṣu padmeṣūpapādukāḥ prādurbhavanti; contrasted with birth in the womb, (anye garbhāvāsaṃ) prativasant, anye (sc. bodhisattvāḥ) punar aupapādukāḥ padmeṣu paryaṅkaiḥ prādurbhavanti (also), some dwell in the dwelling of the womb (, calyx!), others, spontaneously generated, appear sitting cross-legged on lotuses; similarly (na khalu …) bodhisattvā mātāpitṛnirvṛttā bhavanti, atha khalu svaguṇanirvṛttyā (so with mss., by the creative power of their own virtues) upapādukā (v.l. aup˚) bhavanti; in it is explained that Bodhisattvas, after rebirth in the Tuṣita heaven, do not engage in sex relations, and hence Siddhārtha was not Rāhulaʼs father; Rāhula nevertheless entered (in some way not explained) the womb of Yaśodharā; but Rāhula was not aupapāduka as cakravartins are, (rājānaś cakravartinaḥ) aupapādukā babhūvu … cakravartigaṇāḥ [Page163-a] aupapādukā āsan, na tathā Rāhurabhadra iti; that cakravartins are aupa˚ (upa˚) is also shown by (vs, of a cakravartin, having the 32 lakṣaṇa) upapāduko padumagarbhe; cakravartī caturdvīpeśvaraḥ aupapādukaḥ padmagarbhe …; elsewhere however it is clear that one born from the womb may nevertheless be aup˚, yayā (sc. Māyayā) sa upapādukaḥ kumāra (sc. the bodhisattva Śākyamuni) utsaṅge pratigṛhītaḥ; (of a bodhisattva; rājño Vimaladattasya) gṛha upapanna aupapādika (2 mss. ˚duka) utsaṅge paryaṅkeṇa prādurbhūto 'bhūt; other statements about aup˚ (up˚) are that anything they wish is instantly fulfilled, (see s.v. upapāduka) yenopapādukaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ sa(ha)cittotpādāc cāsya yac cintayati yat prārthayate tat sarvaṃ samṛdhyatīti; they have the 32 lakṣaṇa, and otherwise marvelous bodies, (vs) upapādukāḥ sarvi (sc. sattvāḥ) suvarṇavarṇā dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhāriṇaḥ; te sattvā aupapādukā bhaviṣyanti … manomayair ātmabhāvaiḥ svayaṃprabhā(ḥ) …; such birth results from high moral attainments in the past, (striyo yāḥ pañcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ) saṃyojanānāṃ (q.v.) prahāṇād upapādukāḥ; this word is suggested by the letter au in the young Bodhisattvaʼs spelling lesson, aukāre aupapāduka-śabdaḥ.

(see also katira; cf. anyatara; used in this way sometimes in Pali and apparently even in Skt., where however the cases are rare and not always certain), which (of more than two)?:;; kataraḥ (of several) kumāro … rājā bhaviṣyati;; kataraṃ (cited as katarat) cittaṃ; (read kataraṃ tat), 12. In (Ārāḍasya dharmo …) na niryāti tat-katarasya samyagduḥkhakṣayāya, and (nāyaṃ) Ārāḍasya dharmo niryāti tat-katarasya (so mss.) samyagduḥkhakṣayāye, could at best (but implausibly) be taken to mean Ārāḍaʼs religion does not result in the complete destruction of the misery of anyone. But emended to tat-karasya, of (for) the one who performs it (sc. Ārāḍaʼs religion), which is confirmed by Tib. on de byed pa, one who has done that. It is indeed strange to find the same corruption in both texts; but the em. seems quite certain; it is confirmed by Pali takkarassa;, in a quite similar phrase; and in a close parallel one ms. reads tatkarasya (the other corruptly taktenasya).
